WITH invoice_counts AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(i.invoice_number) AS invoice_count
  FROM Orders AS o
  LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY o.order_id
), shares AS (
  SELECT order_id,
         invoice_count,
         1.0 * invoice_count / NULLIF(SUM(invoice_count) OVER (), 0) AS invoice_share
  FROM invoice_counts
), above_average AS (
  SELECT invoice_count,
         invoice_share,
         AVG(invoice_share) OVER () AS average_share
  FROM shares
  WHERE invoice_share > (SELECT AVG(invoice_share) FROM shares)
)
SELECT SUM(invoice_count) AS total_invoices,
       AVG(invoice_share) AS average_share,
       AVG(invoice_share - average_share) AS average_excess_share
FROM above_average;

assumptions.assumption: Orders with no invoices are included when calculating the average share; if there are no invoices at all, the shares are NULL and the result contains one row of NULL aggregates.
